title: Durable provider-run telemetry ledger
description:
SPIDR slice 4 of 4, cut from task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16. This is the PATH slice and the FINAL slice of the family: it owns the durable commit, the full four-leg gate, and the consumer-edge declaration for the whole group.

Hard dependencies: task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16 (record contract), task-fc6581042426444a826981943f441908 (canonical codec) and task-ea27beb6e1954d0e9dba8ad49cc1641e (normalize composition), all DONE.

DELIVERABLE: apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.ts plus its .js bridge and provider-run-ledger.test.ts. Mirror apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts, which is the in-repo template and already encodes every hard decision below.

BEHAVIOUR:
- ONE call to the store's existing commitExpectedVersionDecision through the narrow port declared by slice 1. The durable record IS the event payload - no side table, no bespoke SQLite schema.
- DO NOT reach for commitWithApply or commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply. Those hand the callback a raw DatabaseSync and exist for callers writing their own tables, which the no-new-schema rail forbids. Slice 1's port deliberately does not name them, so the mistake should be unreachable - verify it still is.
- expectedVersion pinned to 0 against the derived aggregate id, so a distinct command targeting a run that already committed observes version 1 and the STORE rejects it. Conflict is borrowed from the aggregate head, never hand-checked.
- REPLAY IS ANSWERED BY READING THE AGGREGATE BACK, NEVER BY ECHOING THE CALLER. This is the defect most likely to ship green in this whole family. The store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array - activation-ledger-commit.ts:16-21 states this outright - so a ledger that returns the caller's own record on REPLAYED makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and pass forever. On disposition REPLAYED, re-read the aggregate and answer from the STORED bytes, verified through the slice-2 decoder.
- Map a thrown store error onto the slice-1 vocabulary while PRESERVING the store's own code verbatim in a separate field. An expected-version conflict and a reused event id are different facts; flattening them destroys a distinction the tests must assert separately.

TESTS use a REAL SqliteEventStore via openEphemeralForProjectTest(projectId) - no fake store. Open the handle inside the it or beforeEach and close it in a finally: a handle opened in a describe body and still held at teardown kills the vitest worker process, which reads as unrelated infrastructure failure rather than as your bug.

MEASURED CONTEXT (re-measure before planning; taken at HEAD 5c5afb1):
- Store public API is sufficient with no new schema: commitExpectedVersionDecision, getCommandDecision(key: CommandDecisionKey), readEvents(aggregateId), readAggregateEvents, openEphemeralForProjectTest. CommandDecisionKey = {commandId, principalId, projectId}. packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts:94.
- Daemon precedent for the same shape: apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts:160-210 and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:206,246.
- Do not publish from apps/daemon/src/index.ts: index-surface.test.ts:267 pins EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length to 61.
- A focused daemon vitest run needs `--root .` or it silently matches ZERO tests and reads exactly like a pass; the package script is `vitest run --root . --config package.json src`.

CONSUMER EDGE: this slice closes the family, so it carries the consumer-edge obligation for all four. task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 is the real live dispatch consumer and MUST be named in the handoff with its id. Check what task-cbc42f3383444c05a20c6bf56129e8c8 already recorded for task-159f4c21 and task-6cbff010 before declaring an edge, so the same edge is not declared twice.

Scope: apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.* only.
definitionOfDone: Exactly one content-bound record is durably committed per provider run through the existing commitExpectedVersionDecision API, with no bespoke SQLite table or schema added, verified by grep showing no CREATE TABLE and no use of the *WithApply commit variants.

A replay of the same commandId with the SAME bytes returns the STORED record read back from the aggregate, not the caller's, and a mutation drill that switches the REPLAYED branch to echo the caller reddens a NAMED test - the drill is mandatory because an echoing implementation passes every other test in this file.
A replay of the same commandId with CHANGED record bytes fails closed with a specific stable reason code naming its layer, and the durable bytes are asserted unchanged afterwards.

A distinct command targeting an already-committed run is rejected on the aggregate head, asserting this module's stable code AND the store's own code preserved verbatim alongside it rather than flattened into one.
Malformed, truncated and digest-mismatched durable reads each return the stable telemetry-unreadable code naming its layer, asserted by code and layer rather than merely that the read failed.

Tests run against a real SqliteEventStore opened per test and closed in a finally, and every added assertion is proven load-bearing by a mutation drill naming the test that reddens, restored and verified by sha256 rather than git diff.

Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner test, pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test, pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test each exit 0 with exit codes read SEPARATELY, and the handoff names task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 as the live dispatch consumer of the composed surface.
taskRails: No new store schema or table; use only the public event/decision transactions and strict canonical bytes. Never call commitWithApply or commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply - they expose a raw DatabaseSync.

Answer REPLAYED by reading the aggregate back, never by echoing the caller's record. The store's replay identity does not cover the events array, so an echo passes every idempotence test while proving nothing.
Preserve the store's own reason code verbatim alongside this module's code; an expected-version conflict and a reused event id are different facts and must stay separately assertable.
Tests use a real SqliteEventStore, never a fake. Open per test and close in a finally - a held handle kills the vitest worker at teardown.
This slice closes the four-slice family and carries the consumer-edge obligation: name task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 in the handoff.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — write the replay-echo killer FIRST, because it is the one defect that ships green. Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.test.ts` against a REAL `SqliteEventStore`, opened per test and closed in a `finally`; a handle held into teardown kills the vitest worker outright. Do not use a fake store: the property under test is the store's own replay identity, and a fake would reimplement exactly the thing being checked.
THE DEFECT, stated so you can aim at it: the store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array (see the note at activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24). So if a replay is answered by echoing the CALLER'S record back, every idempotence assertion compares the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and passes forever — while the ledger has silently stopped reading anything durable. The ONLY test that kills it is the CHANGED-BYTE REPLAY: commit a record, then re-submit the same command key with a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT record body, and assert the answer carries the FIRST record's bytes, read back from the aggregate — not the second's. Write that case before writing the production module, and name it so the step-6 drill can cite it.
Also pin, each asserting the exact `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES` member AND the `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS` member that answered — never merely "refused", because the codec, the store, and this ledger can each refuse and a code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first: a clean first commit; a genuine duplicate of the same run; a record the codec rejects; and a store error surfaced as a refusal. Build every fixture valid at all EARLIER layers so the intended guard is the one that speaks. Assert a positive case count.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.test.ts` from apps/daemon -> EXIT=1, verbatim: "Error: Cannot find module './provider-run-ledger.js'", `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests no tests`. Red for the intended reason (production module absent), not a fixture fault.

THE KILLER, written first and named for the step-5 drill: "refuses a replay whose record drifted, and leaves the durable bytes untouched". Same key, same requestBytes, a record with the same providerRunRef (so the SAME derived aggregate) but sequence.value 3 -> 9. The store replays because its identity covers key/commandKind/targetAggregateId/expectedVersion/requestBytes and NOT the events array. An echoing implementation returns ok here and passes every other assertion in the file.

REAL STORE vs INSTRUMENTED PORT — I had to make a judgement call and I am flagging it rather than burying it. Every replay-identity case drives an unmodified real SqliteEventStore, including the AMBIGUOUS case, which appends its second provider-run event through the store's own `commit` at expectedVersion 1. But the four unreadable/absent read-back cases are UNREACHABLE through any real sequence: the only writer that can leave an event under a REPLAYABLE decision is this ledger, and it only ever writes codec-sealed bytes. So those four use `plantedRead`, which delegates commitExpectedVersionDecision and getCommandDecision to the REAL store and overrides `readEvents` alone. Commit and decision authority stay real; only the bytes the reader finds are chosen. DoD 5 names malformed, truncated and digest-mismatched durable reads explicitly, so the cases are required and this is the least-fake way to reach them. Documented in the test module header.

CASES, each pinning the exact CODE and the exact LAYER (never bare "refused"), 15 tests total:
- first commit: COMMITTED, one event on the derived aggregate, payload byte-equal to the codec's sealed bytes; caller-supplied recordDigest does not survive into the durable bytes; event id deterministic, not the record digest, and different for a different attemptRef.
- identical replay: REPLAYED, digest equal, durable bytes byte-equal, aggregate still holds exactly one event.
- drifted replay: PROVIDER_RUN_REPLAY_DIVERGED / PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER / storeCode null, durable bytes asserted unchanged afterwards.
- foreign event type on the aggregate: still REPLAYED (the type filter is load-bearing, and it must not read a foreign event as ambiguity).
- second provider-run event: PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS / PROVIDER_RUN_READER, outcome UNKNOWN.
- malformed / truncated / digest-mismatched durable bytes: PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE / PROVIDER_RUN_READER / UNKNOWN, with a `expect(UNREADABLE.length).toBe(3)` positive case count so a sweep that generates nothing cannot pass.
- zero provider-run events: PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT / READER. Lone foreign event: PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE_UNEXPECTED / READER.
- distinct command on a committed run: PROVIDER_RUN_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT / PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER with storeCode "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT" preserved verbatim, aggregate still one event.
- codec-rejected record: PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_MALFORMED / PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC returned UNCHANGED, and zero events written.
- closed store: PROVIDER_RUN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE / PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER with storeCode "STORE_CLOSED".
- vocabulary sweep with its own `expect(used.length).toBe(7)` count.

Every store is opened inside its `it` and closed in a `finally` on every exit path including throws.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE COMMIT PATH. Create `provider-run-ledger.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./provider-run-ledger.ts";`, LF ending — apps/daemon REQUIRES a physical bridge per production module and the bridge guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line lands it in `wrongContent`). Mirror `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts:178-212`, which is the reviewed template for this exact shape.
Flow: `encodeProviderRunRecord(input.record)`; on refusal return it unchanged — do NOT re-wrap a codec refusal into a ledger code, that erases which layer refused. Take `const { record } = encoded` and use `encoded.bytes`; the codec MINTS `recordDigest` (codec.ts:156-162, digest domain excludes the field, then seals) so the ledger never computes or supplies one — that is the recorded draft-type decision, already realised in the codec. Derive the aggregate with `deriveProviderRunAggregateId(record.ref)` and call `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision` ONCE with `expectedVersion` pinned to 0, so a second distinct command against an already-committed run observes version 1 and is rejected by the store's own conflict check rather than a hand-rolled one.
THE EVENT ID IS THE ONE GENUINELY OPEN DESIGN POINT — decide it from the store's uniqueness constraints, not by analogy. The activation template COPIES `grantId` and states "minting one here would forfeit the store-wide uniqueness that makes a reused grant refuse"; this family has no pre-existing unique id to copy. Derive one DETERMINISTICALLY from the same five identity facts `deriveProviderRunAggregateId` uses (provider, runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch) under a DISTINCT domain separator — never `randomUUID`, never the `recordDigest` (content-addressed: two identical runs would collide while a changed-byte resubmit would not). Then prove with a test WHICH constraint answers a genuine duplicate: the expectedVersion conflict or `domain_events.event_id` store-wide uniqueness. Both can refuse; the rails require pinning which did.
NEVER call `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`. They hand the callback a raw `DatabaseSync`, which is how the no-new-schema rail gets violated by accident. The `ProviderRunStore` port at contracts.ts:157-162 deliberately names only three methods so those two are unreachable — type against that port, and verify it still omits them.

ANSWER REPLAYED BY READING THE AGGREGATE BACK, AND MAP STORE ERRORS HONESTLY. On a REPLAYED disposition, do NOT return the caller's record. Read the derived aggregate with the port's `readEvents(aggregateId)`, decode the stored payload through `decodeProviderRunRecord`, and answer with THAT — the durable bytes. This is the whole point of step 2's changed-byte case, and it is the module's only other store call. If the read finds no event, or the decode refuses, that is an UNKNOWN, never a success: use `providerRunUnknown` so unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority.
STORE ERROR MAPPING: map onto the slice-1 vocabulary in `provider-run-refusals.ts` while PRESERVING THE STORE'S OWN CODE VERBATIM ALONGSIDE — `provider-run-refusals.ts:16` already imports `DurableStoreErrorCode` from `@moe/store` for exactly this, so the refusal can carry both the ledger's stable code and the store's. Do not collapse a store code into a generic ledger code and discard it; a caller that cannot see which store condition fired cannot distinguish a conflict from a malformed input. Wrap the commit in try/catch and route a thrown error to a refusal rather than letting it escape, mirroring the template's `refuseThrown`.
Keep `provider-run-ledger.ts` under 250 physical lines — measure with `grep -c '' <file>`, since PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts. The siblings run 104-246 lines, so this is comfortable if the module stays a composition of the codec, the derivation and the port rather than re-deriving any of them.

MUTATION DRILLS — epic rail 6, and the first one is mandatory for this task specifically. (1) THE REPLAY-ECHO DRILL: switch the REPLAYED branch to echo the caller's record instead of reading the aggregate back. A NAMED test — the changed-byte replay case from step 2 — MUST go red. Record its name. If it stays green, that assertion is comparing the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and the whole idempotence claim is vacuous; fix the test, not the drill. (2) Change `expectedVersion` from 0 to a value that would accept a second commit, and confirm the duplicate case reddens on its exact code and layer — proving the conflict is borrowed from the store rather than assumed. (3) Make the store-error mapping discard the store's own code and confirm a case reddens — proving the verbatim preservation is asserted, not merely written. (4) Make `deriveProviderRunAggregateId`'s caller pass a constant identity and confirm two distinct runs stop being distinguishable — proving the derivation is load-bearing.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion rather than an unrelated crash — a red for the wrong reason is not a pass. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand — a hand restore goes ambiguous) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next drill; a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit a drill you left on disk.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT. Legs, each run separately with its own captured exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` reading the `Test Files`/`Tests` COUNT LINE, not the exit code — `@moe/daemon` resolves to apps/daemon, and an exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing. Both stay RED from the foreign slices recorded in step 1. Apply the path-attributed baseline: failing paths at HEAD minus failing paths at merge-base, intersected with your three owned files, MUST be empty. Quote the remaining foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths — disclosed, never repaired, never hidden, never fabricated green.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: (a) does every refusal assertion pin BOTH the `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES` member and the answering `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS` member? (b) is REPLAYED answered from `readEvents` + `decodeProviderRunRecord`, with the changed-byte case proving it? (c) is a codec refusal returned unchanged rather than re-wrapped? (d) does the store's own `DurableStoreErrorCode` survive verbatim alongside the ledger code? (e) are `commitWithApply` and `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply` absent from the diff, and does `ProviderRunStore` still omit them? (f) is the event id DETERMINISTIC, with a test naming which constraint refuses a duplicate? (g) is every `SqliteEventStore` closed in a `finally` on every exit path including throws? (h) is `provider-run-ledger.ts` under 250 lines by `grep -c ''`, and does the `.js` bridge carry exactly the one line with an LF? (i) is `apps/daemon/src/index.ts` UNTOUCHED — do not publish from it; index-surface.test.ts:342 pins `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` to 85 (the prior handoff's "61" is stale, re-measure before citing either number). (j) does `git status --porcelain` show only your three owned paths, every drill reverted?
Commit by explicit pathspec naming exactly the three files — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`; the index is shared state in this single working directory. Verify with `git show --stat`. In the completion: quote the count lines verbatim, name the test that reddened for the replay-echo drill, quote the foreign daemon red as disclosure, and state the resolved normalize finding — that no daemon-local normalizer was needed because `buildProviderRunRecord` consumes `normalizeProviderUsage` upstream in @moe/runner. CONSUMER EDGE: name task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 as the live dispatch consumer for this family, but FIRST check what task-cbc42f33 already recorded for task-159f4c21 and task-6cbff010 so the same edge is not declared twice. Keep verification.command under 500 characters.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) FILE A DAEMON-LOCAL NORMALIZE PREREQUISITE and re-block this task, per option (b). REJECTED on measurement: the ledger never normalizes, and task-ea27beb6 was already ARCHIVED with human approval precisely because @moe/runner owns normalization. Filing it would rebuild a landed surface, collide with its owner in a shared worktree, and re-block a slice whose real dependencies are all present.

2) HAVE THE LEDGER CALL `normalizeProviderUsage` ITSELF, per a literal reading of option (a). REJECTED: `buildProviderRunRecord` already calls it (provider-run-record.ts:238), so a second call would either re-normalize already-normalized usage or bypass the runner's composition. The honest form of (a) is that the runner-owned normalization is consumed upstream — which is already true and needs no work here.

3) Take the whole `SqliteEventStore` rather than the `ProviderRunStore` port. REJECTED: contracts.ts:150-156 says this is the only slice that can build the no-new-schema guard and no later test recovers it. Typing against the narrow port is what makes `commitWithApply` structurally unreachable.

4) Answer REPLAYED with the caller's record, which is simpler and needs no second store call. REJECTED — this is THE defect that ships green. The store's replay identity does not cover the events array, so echoing makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes. Only the changed-byte replay case kills it, which is why step 2 writes that case first and step 5 drills it.

5) Mint the event id with `randomUUID`. REJECTED: `domain_events.event_id` is UNIQUE store-wide and that uniqueness is a refusal mechanism. The activation template COPIES `grantId` and says minting "would forfeit the store-wide uniqueness that makes a reused grant refuse." A deterministic identity-derived id preserves that property.

6) Use `recordDigest` as the event id. REJECTED: it is content-addressed, so two genuinely distinct runs with identical content would collide while a changed-byte resubmit of the SAME run would not — exactly inverted from the property wanted.

7) Collapse store errors into generic ledger codes. REJECTED: provider-run-refusals.ts:16 imports `DurableStoreErrorCode` from @moe/store specifically so both codes can travel. A caller that cannot see the store's condition cannot tell a conflict from malformed input.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 6954a8c on 2026-08-16. The governor routed this for an ARCHITECT DECISION between (a) consuming runner-owned normalization and (b) filing a daemon-local normalize prerequisite. The measured answer is NEITHER, and it dissolves the question rather than picking a side.

THE DECISION, measured. This ledger does not normalize at all. `normalizeProviderUsage` is consumed UPSTREAM inside @moe/runner's own `buildProviderRunRecord` — packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/provider-run-record.ts:238 calls it, and provider-usage-normalization.ts:180 defines it. `grep -rn normalizeProviderUsage apps/daemon` returns NOTHING. By the time a `ProviderRunRecord` reaches this ledger it is already composed; the ledger encodes and commits it. So no daemon-local normalize prerequisite should be filed, and normalization the runner already owns must not be rebuilt. This confirms the prior architect's own suspicion, recorded in their handoff openQuestions: "I over-specified the family's dependency prose ... this ledger may not need the normalizer's output directly."

CROSS-PACKAGE EDGE, verified per the workspace-dep rail rather than by a root-barrel grep. (a) apps/daemon/package.json declares `@moe/runner: workspace:*` alongside @moe/contracts, @moe/coordination, @moe/core, @moe/mcp, @moe/review, @moe/scheduler, @moe/store. (c) the compiled probe is ALREADY LANDED AND DURABLE rather than throwaway: `provider-run-contracts.ts:25-38` imports types from the BARE specifier `@moe/runner` and the package typechecks that file today. The plan still has the worker re-confirm the lockfile importer entry.

PREREQUISITE STATE, both directions checked. PRESENT in apps/daemon/src/telemetry/: `provider-run-contracts.ts` (204 lines — `ProviderRunRecord` at 94 including `recordDigest` at 146, the narrow `ProviderRunStore` port at 157, `deriveProviderRunAggregateId` at 201), `provider-run-codec.ts` (246 lines — `encodeProviderRunRecord` 145, `decodeProviderRunRecord` 240) plus `provider-run-codec.validation.ts`, `provider-run-refusals.ts` (104 lines — `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS` 25, `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES` 52, `providerRunRefusal` 89, `providerRunUnknown` 99), each with a `.js` bridge. ABSENT and owned by this task: `provider-run-ledger.{ts,js,test.ts}`. `provider-run-normalize.ts` is absent and stays absent by design.

DIGEST OWNERSHIP is already realised, not merely decided. The codec MINTS `recordDigest`: codec.ts:30 `DIGEST_KEY`, :156 `digest(domain)` over the canonical record with the field EXCLUDED, :157 re-encodes with it set, :159 seals, :162 returns `{bytes, digest, record, ok}`. The ledger therefore never computes or supplies a digest — it takes `encoded.record` and `encoded.bytes`, exactly as the activation template does.

THE NARROW PORT IS A DELIBERATE GUARD. contracts.ts:150-162 states it: `commitWithApply` and `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply` are absent BY CONSTRUCTION because `CommitApply` hands out a raw `DatabaseSync`, which the no-new-schema rail forbids, and "a port that cannot NAME them cannot reach for them ... no later test recovers it." Type against `ProviderRunStore`, never against `SqliteEventStore`.

THE AGGREGATE DERIVATION is done and heavily documented (contracts.ts:165-204): UTF-8-length-framed, domain-separated SHA-256 over five identity facts, fixed size because a producer-admitted ref can carry three 200-byte fields and the store's identifier ceiling is 512 bytes. Its own doc warns it VALIDATES NOTHING — the runner withholds `snapshotRunRef` from its package root, so callers must take the ref from a validated handoff.

planningNotes.risks:
1) THE REPLAY-ECHO DEFECT IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS GREEN, and it is the reason this task is worth planning carefully at all. The store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array (activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24). Answering REPLAYED with the caller's own record makes every idempotence assertion tautological and passes forever. Only the CHANGED-BYTE replay case kills it. Write that case first; drill it; require a NAMED red.

2) NEVER `commitWithApply` / `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`. They hand out a raw `DatabaseSync` and are how the no-new-schema rail gets violated by accident. The port deliberately cannot name them — verify it still cannot.

3) A HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER. Real `SqliteEventStore` only, opened per test, closed in a `finally` on every exit path including throws.

4) apps/daemon REQUIRES a physical `.js` bridge per production module, and the bridge guard BYTE-COMPARES. One line, LF ending; CRLF or a trailing blank line lands the file in `wrongContent` rather than fixing `missing`.

5) DO NOT PUBLISH FROM apps/daemon/src/index.ts. index-surface.test.ts:342 pins `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` to 85 — note the prior handoff's "61" is STALE, so re-measure before citing any number. index.ts is not an owned path here.

6) THE DAEMON GATES ARE RED AT BASELINE from foreign in-flight slices (review-acceptance, agent-spawner, d92 parked TDD reds). Record the before-set precisely; the path-attributed delta over your three owned files is what must be empty. Do not repair foreign reds and do not narrow a leg to hide one.

7) EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. Read the `Test Files`/`Tests` count line. Never `;`-chain a gate (only the last status survives) and never pipe into tail (tail's status is reported).

8) THREE LAYERS CAN REFUSE — the codec, the store, and this ledger. An assertion pinning only a code, or only "refused", detaches the moment a different layer answers first. Pin code AND layer, and build each fixture valid at every earlier layer.

9) `deriveProviderRunAggregateId` VALIDATES NOTHING, by its own documentation. Hashing a caller-forged ref does not make it trustworthy; the ref must come from a validated handoff, and the complete identity stays inside the record for later readers to compare rather than treating hash uniqueness as authority.

10) SHARED WORKTREE, ACTIVE. HEAD moved many times during this session. Re-check `git status --porcelain` immediately before committing, commit by explicit three-path pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`, confirm every drill reverted.

11) CONSUMER-EDGE DOUBLE-DECLARATION. This slice carries the family's consumer-edge obligation — name task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 — but check what task-cbc42f33 already recorded for task-159f4c21 and task-6cbff010 first, so the same edge is not declared twice.
